currentContext.strengths: Largest Ayurvedic company in India and worldwide with a repertoire of products built on the principles of Ayurveda|Household penetration - present in nearly 8 out of 10 Indian households, described as a key differentiator in a highly competitive market|Portfolio of heritage trusted brands such as Dabur Chyawanprash, Dabur Honey and Dabur Glucose that outperformed category growth and gained market share|Deep rural presence and an expanding retail footprint into newer villages|Natural, science-backed product-led portfolio aligned to rising consumer preference for natural ingredients|Global footprint with presence in more than 120 countries and manufacturing across nine countries|Highest-grade credit standing - long-term rating AAA (Stable) and short-term A1+ reaffirmed by both CRISIL and ICRA|Group governance framework including a Policy on Group Governance covering unlisted subsidiaries globally
currentContext.strategies: Continue strengthening the core categories and heritage brands rooted in nature, science and consumer well-being|Invest in innovation and accelerate premiumisation, including new-age formats and premium variants|Unlock new growth vectors in e-commerce and quick commerce channels, the fastest-growing route to consumers|Reinvent Go-to-Market with GTM 2.0 through Project Saksham|Drive disciplined cost optimisation through Project Samriddhi|Leverage digital capabilities to transform the entire value chain|Explore strategic M&A opportunities for portfolio diversification and acceleration|Deploy Dabur Ventures, a Rs 500 crore platform, to invest in high-potential new-age digital-first brands, starting with a stake in RAS Beauty Private Limited|Build future-ready domestic manufacturing capacity, signalled by the new facility at Tindivanam, Tamil Nadu|Build a future-ready, digitally enabled enterprise through Global Capability Centres - an IT GCC already operational and a Digital Marketing GCC being set up|Scale a centralized AI framework to identify, prioritise and deploy AI use cases across Sales, Marketing, Commercial and Supply Chain|Strengthen international brands, expand distribution and build platforms for long-term sustainable growth across a footprint of over 120 countries|Grow responsibly - environmental stewardship, responsible sourcing, sustainable herb cultivation and farmer livelihoods|Dabur frames capital allocation within its governance philosophy of long-term value creation and protection of stakeholder interests, citing uninterrupted dividend payments and high credit ratings among the returns from strong governance practices. Dividends are declared in accordance with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy framed under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations and the Companies Act, 2013, with an interim dividend paid during the year and a final dividend recommended for member approval; no amount is proposed to be transferred to reserves. Unpaid or unclaimed dividends outstanding for seven years are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund. Reinvestment intent is expressed through building future-ready domestic manufacturing capacity and portfolio expansion, including the pending amalgamation of Sesa Care Private Limited, while a Policy on Group Governance monitors the governance of unlisted subsidiaries across the globe.|Recognised as a Water Positive Enterprise, achieving water positivity four years ahead of its 2030 target, through operational efficiency within Company facilities combined with conservation and groundwater recharge initiatives in surrounding communities|Environmental stewardship, responsible sourcing and community development are positioned as integral to how the Company operates and grows|Support for sustainable herb cultivation and farmer livelihoods as part of the responsible sourcing agenda|Fulfilment of environmental, social and governance responsibility is stated as an integral part of how the Company conducts business, with a Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report published under Regulation 34 of the Listing Regulations
currentContext.expansion: India: FY 2025-26 saw Dabur break ground for a new greenfield site at Tindivanam, Tamil Nadu, with the formal ground-breaking ceremony conducted by the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu in February 2026, after which construction started in full swing; the factory is expected to begin operations by end of FY 2026-27 with Red Toothpaste and Gulabari, and more lines and product categories are to be added in future. Overseas, Dabur runs a localised supply chain with eight manufacturing facilities located in UAE, Egypt, Turkey, Nigeria, South Africa, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, and an overall manufacturing presence across nine countries serving a footprint of more than 120 countries. UAE: the integrated RAK unit makes hair, oral and skin care with a capacity of over 70,000 MT / 9.5 million cases of finished goods annually and caters to more than 70 countries; during the year Kaizen initiatives, low-cost automation and packaging line de-bottlenecking lifted line speeds and delivered a 3% year-on-year productivity improvement, and the plant commissioned a state-of-the-art effluent treatment plant designed to cut incoming COD of 20,000 mg/l to under 50 mg/l with treated water reused for landscaping and plant operations. Egypt: the Cairo facility making Dabur, Vatika and ORS hair, oral and skin care for domestic and export markets enhanced production capacity for oral care and shampoo, is creating capacity for Hobby Body Wash and Herbolene, and has operationalised phase 1 of a new greenfield plant in 10th of Ramadan City alongside energy-saving technology, expanded solar adoption and automation. Nigeria: the Lagos factory added a second hair care line, significantly increasing production capacity, began in-house production of lotion in bottle format, wrap set mousse and hair lotion, launched Clove Gel and Charcoal toothpaste, achieved AEO certification and completed a TUV audit with a score exceeding 98%, and serves as an export hub for West African ECOWAS markets. South Africa: the Johannesburg plant, which locally produces 90% of the country's volume, delivered annual in-house production of over 240k cases plus 114k outsourced cases, added a new factory warehouse, automation enhancements and safety projects, and has become a sourcing centre for multiple markets under the SSA framework. Turkey: the Hobi Kozmetik factory near Istanbul, with manufacturing capacity of 55,000 MT per annum of liquid soaps, shampoos, conditioners, hair care, bodywash and skin care, received major investment during the year to raise shampoo and bodywash output for export markets, increase automation in shampoo and liquid soap production, and expand cap and jar production. Distribution and retail expansion: Dabur served 8.5 million outlets during the year, becoming the No. 2 most distributed FMCG company in India, and grew direct reach to 1.52 million outlets, an increase of 100,000 outlets over FY 2024-25, alongside a GTM transformation extending channel programmes to Open Format Outlets, A-Class Grocers, Chemists and Eateries & Dining outlets. NewU, the beauty retail chain run by wholly owned subsidiary H & B Stores Limited, added 14 new stores during FY 2025-26 to reach 105 stores across 55 cities, continuing a FOCO (Franchise-Owned, Company-Operated) expansion model, with private labels Jaquline USA, Botanica and London Notes contributing around 22% of NewU sales. In the US ethnic business, 18 new SKUs were launched and a Walmart U.S. listing was secured for Dabur Amla with two SKUs across 1,200 stores, with further vertical and horizontal expansion planned across the U.S. and Canada.
currentContext.mdna: India remained one of the world's fastest-growing major economies, with real GDP for FY 2025-26 estimated by the RBI to grow by 7.6%, driven by robust private consumption and public investment in infrastructure|GST rate rationalisation and income tax rate cuts are expected to further enhance disposable incomes, stimulate demand and support consumption-led growth|Rural demand remained resilient on favourable agricultural performance and an above-normal monsoon, continuing to trend ahead of urban markets|Urban consumption was initially subdued but showed gradual recovery in the latter part of the year, driven by quick commerce, modern trade and e-commerce|Supportive fiscal measures and improving urban sentiment are expected to drive a more broad-based recovery in FMCG demand|Global uncertainties and energy price volatility remain key watchpoints after the outbreak of war in early 2026 disrupted oil supply chains and triggered inflationary pressures worldwide|Unseasonal rains and erratic weather during peak summer months tempered demand for seasonal categories and disrupted consumption|Margin levers cited by management: judicious price increases, a sharper focus on premiumisation and disciplined cost management|Premiumisation is working - premium Chyawanprash variants Dabur Ratnaprash and Dabur Gur Chyawanprash recorded double-digit growth, and Organic and Sundarbans Honey grew 2x year-on-year|E-commerce is a structural growth driver, with Dabur Honey e-commerce sales touching Rs 100 crore during the year|International business remains a key growth pillar spanning over 120 countries, supported by a diversified footprint, strong local execution and a resilient supply chain|Enterprise AI platform and AI-led demand forecasting, pricing and trade promotion optimisation are being used to lift productivity and investment efficiency

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and energy price volatility
risks.note: The outbreak of war in early 2026 disrupted oil supply chains, drove up energy prices and triggered inflationary pressures worldwide; uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz and financial tightening slowed growth, and management flags global uncertainties and energy price volatility as key watchpoints for FMCG demand and input costs.

risks.risk: Weather volatility and seasonality of key categories
risks.note: Unseasonal rains and erratic weather, particularly during peak summer months, tempered demand for seasonal categories; consumption in the healthcare portfolio and brands such as Dabur Glucose was explicitly impacted by unseasonal rains and a shorter summer.

risks.risk: Soft urban demand in traditional trade
risks.note: Urban demand, particularly in traditional trade, remained under pressure in the first half of the year and recovered only slowly, making a large part of the India FMCG business dependent on a gradual and uncertain urban recovery.

risks.risk: Channel disruption from e-commerce and quick commerce
risks.note: The expansion of e-commerce and quick commerce is rapidly reshaping buying behaviour and channel salience, requiring continual re-engineering of route-to-market, assortment and trade economics to avoid losing share in a shifting retail landscape.

Dabur describes operating in a highly competitive market where consumer connect is the key differentiator; sustaining market share gains depends on continued brand investment, innovation and premiumisation.

Global inflation is expected to inch up significantly on the Middle East war situation; the Company relies on judicious price increases, premiumisation and cost management, which may lag if input inflation accelerates.

risks.risk: International business exposure across more than 120 countries
risks.note: Dabur has manufacturing presence across nine countries and sells in more than 120, exposing the consolidated business to currency movement, geopolitical complexity in certain regions and trade or tariff policy shifts.

risks.risk: Dependence on rural demand and the agricultural cycle
risks.note: Rural demand, which trended ahead of urban markets, was aided by favourable agricultural performance, an above-normal monsoon, government welfare initiatives and GST rationalisation - a reversal in any of these would directly affect Dabur's rural-weighted portfolio.

one-line thesis: Dabur India reported 6.1% consolidated revenue growth in Q3FY26, driven by a post-GST transition demand recovery and strong rural performance, with operating profit expanding 7.7% despite a one-time labor law provision. Management guides for high single-digit growth in Q4 and a return to ~20% operating margins in FY27 as input costs soften and deferred price hikes roll over.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +6.1% YoY (Domestic FMCG +6%, Vol +3%); EBITDA/Op Profit: +7.7% YoY (Margin expansion despite one-off); PAT (Reported): +10.1% YoY; PAT (Normalized): +7.2% YoY (adjusted for one-time labor law provision); Order Book: N/A (FMCG); Net Debt: Not explicitly detailed, but capital allocation focused on reinvestment.
guidance: Revenue Growth: High single-digit for Q4FY26; High single-to-low double-digit for FY27; Margin: Sequential improvement expected; FY27 target to return to ~20% operating margin; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: Reinvestment of gross margin upside into advertising (75-80%) and margin expansion (20-25%).
order book & pipeline: N/A for FMCG business model; focus on trade inventory liquidation completed for Chyawanprash and Beverages to enable fresh billing.
segment / subsidiary detail: HPC +10.6% (Hair Oil +19.1%, Shampoo +6.2%); Oral Care +10% (Meswak/Herbal +25%); Home Care (Odonil double-digit); Healthcare (Honey +10%, Chyawanprash flat primary but +11% offtake); Digestives +7%; Beverages (Real Activ +38%, Coconut Water +52%); International +11% INR (+7.5% CC).
growth verticals / optionality: Premiumization in Chyawanprash (Gur/Ratnaprash/Sugar-free growing 2-3x core); New Product Developments (Ghee +33%, Edible Oils +50%, Health Juices +18%); Rural market penetration narrowing gap with urban.
margins & cost dynamics: Input costs (Coconut oil, SLES, Vegetable oils) softening after spikes; Q3 PAT impacted by one-time labor law provision; FY27 margin expansion planned via passing on 20-25% of gross margin upside to operating profit while reinvesting rest in A&P; 2% price increase planned for Q4 carry-forward.
capex / expansion: No specific greenfield capex mentioned; strategy focuses on rationalizing tail products and investing in brand building and distribution expansion.
capital allocation: Prioritizing reinvestment of cost savings into consumer communication (A&P) to drive volume; balancing margin expansion with market share gains.
risks & watch-items: Weather dependency for Beverage/Glucose segments; Regulatory surprises (e.g., labor codes); Competitive intensity in modern trade (Oral Care); Geopolitical/tariff impacts on exports.
management quality / tone: Optimistic on sequential demand recovery; cautious on weather-dependent categories; confident in margin restoration to 20% levels; transparent about one-offs and inventory corrections.
non-obvious takeaways: Chyawanprash primary sales were flat due to deliberate avoidance of pre-season loading to clear legacy trade inventory, masking strong 11% tertiary offtake; Hair Oil growth is largely value-driven (price) due to prior coconut oil inflation, whereas Oral Care is increasingly volume-driven; 2% price hike deferred due to anti-profiteering norms will roll over in Q4/FY27.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Dabur India Limited is the largest Ayurvedic company in India and worldwide, building trusted natural, science-backed health and personal care brands that reach nearly 8 out of 10 Indian households.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Dabur makes and markets Ayurveda- and nature-based consumer products spanning health and wellness, everyday personal care and value-added foods and beverages. The business is organised into three Strategic Business Units - Consumer Care (Health Care plus Home & Personal Care), Food & Beverages (fruit-based beverages, foods and the acquired Badshah Masala portfolio) and International Business (organic overseas operations plus the acquired Hobi Group and Namaste Laboratories LLC). Consumer Care and Food & Beverages together form the India FMCG business, sold through traditional trade, modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce channels across urban and rural India.

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India FMCG - rural markets with deep village-level distribution
- India FMCG - urban markets via traditional trade, modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce
- International markets: presence in more than 120 countries worldwide
- Indian households seeking Ayurvedic, natural health and wellness products

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A for FMCG business model; focus on trade inventory liquidation completed for Chyawanprash and Beverages to enable fresh billing.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: High single-digit for Q4FY26; High single-to-low double-digit for FY27; Margin: Sequential improvement expected; FY27 target to return to ~20% operating margin; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: Reinvestment of gross margin upside into advertising (75-80%) and margin expansion (20-25%).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Premiumization in Chyawanprash (Gur/Ratnaprash/Sugar-free growing 2-3x core); New Product Developments (Ghee +33%, Edible Oils +50%, Health Juices +18%); Rural market penetration narrowing gap with urban.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remained one of the world's fastest-growing major economies, with real GDP for FY 2025-26 estimated by the RBI to grow by 7.6%, driven by robust private consumption and public investment in infrastructure
- GST rate rationalisation and income tax rate cuts are expected to further enhance disposable incomes, stimulate demand and support consumption-led growth
- Rural demand remained resilient on favourable agricultural performance and an above-normal monsoon, continuing to trend ahead of urban markets
- Urban consumption was initially subdued but showed gradual recovery in the latter part of the year, driven by quick commerce, modern trade and e-commerce
- Supportive fiscal measures and improving urban sentiment are expected to drive a more broad-based recovery in FMCG demand
- Global uncertainties and energy price volatility remain key watchpoints after the outbreak of war in early 2026 disrupted oil supply chains and triggered inflationary pressures worldwide
- Unseasonal rains and erratic weather during peak summer months tempered demand for seasonal categories and disrupted consumption
- Margin levers cited by management: judicious price increases, a sharper focus on premiumisation and disciplined cost management
- Premiumisation is working - premium Chyawanprash variants Dabur Ratnaprash and Dabur Gur Chyawanprash recorded double-digit growth, and Organic and Sundarbans Honey grew 2x year-on-year
- E-commerce is a structural growth driver, with Dabur Honey e-commerce sales touching Rs 100 crore during the year
- International business remains a key growth pillar spanning over 120 countries, supported by a diversified footprint, strong local execution and a resilient supply chain
- Enterprise AI platform and AI-led demand forecasting, pricing and trade promotion optimisation are being used to lift productivity and investment efficiency

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Input costs (Coconut oil, SLES, Vegetable oils) softening after spikes; Q3 PAT impacted by one-time labor law provision; FY27 margin expansion planned via passing on 20-25% of gross margin upside to operating profit while reinvesting rest in A&P; 2% price increase planned for Q4 carry-forward.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing reinvestment of cost savings into consumer communication (A&P) to drive volume; balancing margin expansion with market share gains.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: India: FY 2025-26 saw Dabur break ground for a new greenfield site at Tindivanam, Tamil Nadu, with the formal ground-breaking ceremony conducted by the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu in February 2026, after which construction started in full swing; the factory is expected to begin operations by end of FY 2026-27 with Red Toothpaste and Gulabari, and more lines and product categories are to be added in future. Overseas, Dabur runs a localised supply chain with eight manufacturing facilities located in UAE, Egypt, Turkey, Nigeria, South Africa, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, and an overall manufacturing presence across nine countries serving a footprint of more than 120 countries. UAE: the integrated RAK unit makes hair, oral and skin care with a capacity of over 70,000 MT / 9.5 million cases of finished goods annually and caters to more than 70 countries; during the year Kaizen initiatives, low-cost automation and packaging line de-bottlenecking lifted line speeds and delivered a 3% year-on-year productivity improvement, and the plant commissioned a state-of-the-art effluent treatment plant designed to cut incoming COD of 20,000 mg/l to under 50 mg/l with treated water reused for landscaping and plant operations. Egypt: the Cairo facility making Dabur, Vatika and ORS hair, oral and skin care for domestic and export markets enhanced production capacity for oral care and shampoo, is creating capacity for Hobby Body Wash and Herbolene, and has operationalised phase 1 of a new greenfield plant in 10th of Ramadan City alongside energy-saving technology, expanded solar adoption and automation. Nigeria: the Lagos factory added a second hair care line, significantly increasing production capacity, began in-house production of lotion in bottle format, wrap set mousse and hair lotion, launched Clove Gel and Charcoal toothpaste, achieved AEO certification and completed a TUV audit with a score exceeding 98%, and serves as an export hub for West African ECOWAS markets. South Africa: the Johannesburg plant, which locally produces 90% of the country's volume, delivered annual in-house production of over 240k cases plus 114k outsourced cases, added a new factory warehouse, automation enhancements and safety projects, and has become a sourcing centre for multiple markets under the SSA framework. Turkey: the Hobi Kozmetik factory near Istanbul, with manufacturing capacity of 55,000 MT per annum of liquid soaps, shampoos, conditioners, hair care, bodywash and skin care, received major investment during the year to raise shampoo and bodywash output for export markets, increase automation in shampoo and liquid soap production, and expand cap and jar production. Distribution and retail expansion: Dabur served 8.5 million outlets during the year, becoming the No. 2 most distributed FMCG company in India, and grew direct reach to 1.52 million outlets, an increase of 100,000 outlets over FY 2024-25, alongside a GTM transformation extending channel programmes to Open Format Outlets, A-Class Grocers, Chemists and Eateries & Dining outlets. NewU, the beauty retail chain run by wholly owned subsidiary H & B Stores Limited, added 14 new stores during FY 2025-26 to reach 105 stores across 55 cities, continuing a FOCO (Franchise-Owned, Company-Operated) expansion model, with private labels Jaquline USA, Botanica and London Notes contributing around 22% of NewU sales. In the US ethnic business, 18 new SKUs were launched and a Walmart U.S. listing was secured for Dabur Amla with two SKUs across 1,200 stores, with further vertical and horizontal expansion planned across the U.S. and Canada.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Optimistic on sequential demand recovery; cautious on weather-dependent categories; confident in margin restoration to 20% levels; transparent about one-offs and inventory corrections.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest Ayurvedic company in India and worldwide with a repertoire of products built on the principles of Ayurveda
- Household penetration - present in nearly 8 out of 10 Indian households, described as a key differentiator in a highly competitive market
- Portfolio of heritage trusted brands such as Dabur Chyawanprash, Dabur Honey and Dabur Glucose that outperformed category growth and gained market share
- Deep rural presence and an expanding retail footprint into newer villages
- Natural, science-backed product-led portfolio aligned to rising consumer preference for natural ingredients
- Global footprint with presence in more than 120 countries and manufacturing across nine countries
- Highest-grade credit standing - long-term rating AAA (Stable) and short-term A1+ reaffirmed by both CRISIL and ICRA
- Group governance framework including a Policy on Group Governance covering unlisted subsidiaries globally

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Weather dependency for Beverage/Glucose segments; Regulatory surprises (e.g., labor codes); Competitive intensity in modern trade (Oral Care); Geopolitical/tariff impacts on exports.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Chyawanprash primary sales were flat due to deliberate avoidance of pre-season loading to clear legacy trade inventory, masking strong 11% tertiary offtake; Hair Oil growth is largely value-driven (price) due to prior coconut oil inflation, whereas Oral Care is increasingly volume-driven; 2% price hike deferred due to anti-profiteering norms will roll over in Q4/FY27.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue strengthening the core categories and heritage brands rooted in nature, science and consumer well-being
- Invest in innovation and accelerate premiumisation, including new-age formats and premium variants
- Unlock new growth vectors in e-commerce and quick commerce channels, the fastest-growing route to consumers
- Reinvent Go-to-Market with GTM 2.0 through Project Saksham
- Drive disciplined cost optimisation through Project Samriddhi
- Leverage digital capabilities to transform the entire value chain
- Explore strategic M&A opportunities for portfolio diversification and acceleration
- Deploy …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Market share] The deck claims 90% of the portfolio gained market shares in FY26.
- [International] International Business grew by 6.2% in constant-currency terms in FY26; the FY26 international revenue breakdown is Middle East 27%, Africa 23%, Asia 19%, Europe 16% and Americas 15%.
- [AI] DaburGPT is presented as an internal AI tool "Empowering Smarter Decisions Across Functions" - enhancing productivity through AI-enabled insights, automation and collaboration, and supporting faster decision-making, with AI leveraged across the Dabur value chain.
- [Route to market] Local-event marketing (melas, festivals, Durga Puja, Ramleela, trade fairs and elections) plus print media and wall painting remain explicit visibility levers alongside digital.
- [Deck context] This is the presentation made to shareholders at the 51st Annual General Meeting held on August 06, 2026, delivered by Mohit Malhotra, CEO - it is an AGM deck, not a standard quarterly results deck.
